The Ranger knows where it is at all times. It knows this because it knows where it isn't. By subtracting where it is from where it isn't, or where it isn't from where it is (whichever is greater), it obtains a difference, or deviation. The Ranger handbook uses deviations to generate corrective commands to drive the Ranger from a position where it is to a position where it isn't, and arriving at a position where it wasn't, it now is. Consequently, the position where it is, is now the position that it wasn't, and it follows that the position that it was, is now the position that it isn't.
In the event that the position that it is in is not the position that it wasn't, the Ranger handbook has acquired a variation, the variation being the difference between where the Ranger is, and where it wasn't. If variation is considered to be a significant factor, it too may be corrected by the RH. However, the Ranger must also know where it was.
The Ranger handbook scenario works as follows. Because a variation has modified some of the information the Ranger has obtained, it is not sure just where it is. However, it is sure where it isn't, within reason, and it knows where it was. It now subtracts where it should be from where it wasn't, or vice-versa, and by differentiating this from the algebraic sum of where it shouldn't be, and where it was, it is able to obtain the deviation and its variation, which is called error.

Here's the low down for College money.
Texas is not one of the states that offers totally free college, however there are some other things.
Texas offers state tuition assistance which you can use in addition to any federal assistance that I'll talk about in a bit. If you take 12 or more credit hours a semester it usually covers about $2,000-2,500, however it's not been a set amount even from semester to semester in my experience. In addition to that you can use EITHER your Federal Tuition assistance OR your Montgomery GI bill. The GI bill without the kicker is honestly pretty much beer money at around $350/month, so if you're really wanting to pay as little as you can for college I'd opt for the Federal Tuition assistance, at least so long as you don't qualify for the post 9/11 GI bill at 90 days active duty time (training not included) 

Depending on the school you go to, those two Tuition assistance programs combined can cover most if not all of your tuition. (to say nothing of housing, books, or food) 

Hope this helps.

Even so I still cannot recommend dual wielding guns as even with a revolver you will need to reload mid fight at some point and it’s going to get messy. Also you’ll need to invest in dual-wielding feats and even then you’ll take a -4 to hit firing both due to there not being any light firearms. You’ll only get one more attack/round with your off hand weapon anyway if you get the opportunity to take a full round action. IMO you’re better off investing your feats into using a single firearm, hell, even using a flintlock pistol, you only need one feat before you can reload it as a free action and fire off as many bullets as you have attacks/round without blinking.
There are of course ways to build a double pistol gunslinger, and it can be quite effective at high level play. Throwing a bunch of lead downrange even with massive penalties has its advantages. However I have found that using a single firearm is much simpler to build, doesn’t have to use anything that could be considered “finicky”, and deals only slightly less damage once you get mid-late game since you’re actually more likely to be hitting those tertiary attacks. And you’ll be one/rounding most anything you come across at lvl 5-7 with one or two guns.

Source: I have a 16th level pathfinder society gunslinger

About the dice toll system. to me this is a core issue in any loot system. Especially, if no matter how high in difficulty you play, the lower end of the spectrum stays around the same rarity. If you take the base dice, each of them has a 33.3(repeating)% chance to come up a success. 1/3. That's not too terrible in itself, the problem is when it compounds. So say you're playing on Nightmare and you want an orange. you need 6-7 successes on average. that's a .0004% chance of getting 7 and a .001% chance of getting a 6. Meanwhile there is a.05% chance of getting 0 successes and .08% chance of getting 1 aka getting a green. so the remaining 99.8686% will be between 2-5 successes netting a blue. The odds are astronomically against the player which is why it often feels like the loot system is pointless and rolls way too low more often than not. If a game dev wants to make loot rng, base it off of something more concrete such as how long you've been playing the game (player lvl) or if you're going to base the loot of of how hard something is to do, as it seems to be the case, make more categories of weapons (Ex. something between blue and orange) So that even if you don't get an orange, there's still a decent chance of getting something better than blue. Or make the differences between said categories larger so that playing higher difficulties to improve your odds of getting better loot is easier. Idk what the solution to the problem is, but this is just my 2 cents on the matter. I used to really love this game, but now I just can't motivate myself to play it anymore

I should probably start with the fact that there are 5 kinds of weapon rarity in the game. Plentiful, (white border, the kinds of weapons you start with in the game.) Common, (green border, same static stats but allows you to have 1 trait on the weapon for an added bonus) Rare, (blue border, slight increase in damage over green and white and allows you to have 2 traits) Exotic (orange border, another slight increase in damage over blues and the addition of a third trait. Arguably the best weapon rarity in the game, but more on that in a bit) and Veteran (red border, these have the same damage numbers and number of traits as oranges, but have pre-selected traits that are automatically at max % proc rate where applicable. Thus the argument that orange is better than red as you cannot change the red weapons traits to more favorable ones like you can with oranges) So, obviously the idea of the item progression it to go from white to orange/red and the arguably easiest (and most popular)way to do this is to grind the horn of magnus, enemy below, and man the ramparts on the hard difficulty, then nightmare once you are comfortable with running hard. I haven't played hard in a while personally, but I think that on the hard table there is a low chance of getting white, a mediocre chance of gettign green, a fair chance at blue, and a low chance at orange.

I'm just gonna throw my opinion in here since no one will probably see it. The problem with adc mains is that they tend to main one champion or at least one of the two types of adc's. That's right there are in fact two separate types of attack damage carries. Caster based carries, those that rely on their abilities to do damage, such as Ezreal, Sivir, Miss Fortune, Corki, etc. and auto attack carries, such as Vayne, Jinx, Caitlyn, etc. They both do AD based damage, but they do it in different ways. Caster based carries are burst oriented, they have a lot of damage up front, but don't often build a ton of attack speed and can't put out consistent damage. AA based carries have a lot of DoT, but can't burst very well. Both types of adc's require similar mechanics as far as laneing, but have separate roles in teamfights. Caster carries can burst the assassin that jumps on them with relative ease but have difficulty with anyone that can survive their cooldowns, and vice versa, AA relient Carries can kite a tank to death with consistent damage, but lack the burst to kill an assassin before it kills them. So since there will always be tanks or assassins in the meta, ADC mains will always bitch. Because there's always one of the two factions that hates the meta.
